chapter: Harlem, Redman's band and the Savoy
title: The Casino de Paris show with Redman and Ben Pollack
summary: In 1933 Redman's band shared Billy Rose's Casino de Paris show with Ben Pollack's band, whose members included Spivak, Yank Lawson and Eddie Miller.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: So going back to 1933 with Don Redmon, after that

year of one-nighters, we played the first theater restaurant in New York. It was called the Casino de Paris. It was where theater -- CBS Theater number four is now on 54th Street. That was the Casino de Paris. Billy Rose was the manager and he run it for the Kings Beer people. In those days it was the Kings Beer people, if you understand.
: Sure.

A beautiful show. Two bands, Ben Pollack's band and Don Redmon. And we used to play the show together. The conductor was Charlie Drury, he used to conduct the show and he used to have a light that he would stand in the middle and he would conduct both bands. Sometimes both bands would be playing at the same time in the show.
: Oh, I see.
Ben Pollack had a very good band. And we started --
: You remember the guys who was in that band, Butter?
Well, I remember Charlie Spivak was in that band. He was playing first trumpet. Yank Lawson was in that band. Eddie Miller was the tenor player.
: Wow.
Ray Bauduc was the drummer. And Joe Harris. He only had one trombone. Joe Harris was the
trombone player. He later went to California. And I think Bob Zurkee was playing the piano and I think Bobby Haggart was playing the bass. I think he was playing the bass then.
Bob Haggart?
Yeah, uh-huh.
It was a band actually later that Bob Crosby took over.
Oh, it became the Bobcats?
That's right.
I see. Now what year was that again, just to -- ?
That was 1933, but the Bobcats didn't come into being, I think, till about '36 or '37 --
Right.
-- when Ben Pollôck --
